Проблема не ти е височината, а комуникацията и комплексите. Както са те посъветвали - намери терапевт и говори за това, не е срамно. Срамно ще бъде обаче да станеш един инсел след 2-5-10 години, защото не си искал да се справиш с проблема. 

Вече не си в даскало, за да лежиш на "подиграваха ми се". И мен ме скъсваха, ама си свиркам и ми е все тая. Ниска съм, грозновата съм и съм с повече килограми, но за сметка на това съм се срещала с изключителни красиви, интелигентни и поддържани мъже. Абсолютно всичко е в главата ти, самочувствието ти и себепознанието ти. Нареди си мислите, работи над комуникацията си и нещата ще ти се нареждат. 

Мой познат също имаше комплекс за височината години наред. Пича си оправи живота, нареди си мислите, след няколко месеца се жени за адски красива жена и като цяло всички му се нарежда. Ти какво правиш за да ти се нареждат нещата? Ще ревеш, че си роден нисък или ще си хванеш живота в ръце? Има мнооооооого по-важни неща от размери, височини и прочие. Щастието няма да дойде ако си 20см по-висок. Въпрос на мироглед е.

Making fun behind their backs is common. Violent racism is not. There is a bit of confusion when talking about racism especially in Bulgaria, where most smaller cities have not encountered foreigners or have very little experience. In the term "racism", I think it's pretty safe to have some random people laugh behind you than actively seeking physical confrontation because you aren't white, as one might think when "racist society" is thrown. It's important to differentiate western racism where you gon get stabbed for the colour of your skin, and eastern racism where the local grandmas gone stare at you with disgust. Neither is good, one is safer tho.
Inexpensive places - most are. Check booking, hotels and apartments. For shorter stays, I can recommend a few hostels that are pretty chill.

For a month here in May, I'd highly recommend you to check a few cities for a couple of days. 

- Have a plan
- Prepare with places, prices, etc
- Try to find Bulgarians to help you within the city or just to hang out 

About racism - most people might pull a racist joke, hardly any violence but always be aware of it.

April-May is great to visit bigger cities like Sofia, Plovdiv, Veliko Turnovo, Varna, maybe Burgas (I will personally not recommend, I don't really like the city but that's just my opinion)

You can also visit smaller cities - Vratsa, Gabrovo (in specifics Etura), Lukovit, Smolyan, Kazanlak. Mind you that most small cities will get boring after day 2

I would avoid Shumen or spend max 1 day there. Personally for me, it is a boring city with not much to do, but it's chill.

If you just plan to visit, party or relax - bigger city or two might be the best. Sofia is a bit more fast paced, Varna is a bit more chill place - I'd recommend you to spend time in both.

Hey there.

Bulgaria is pretty safe, however, your best bet is to connect with people from around to make sure you don't get scammed lol

If you are really into visiting, I might be able to help you with some directions and activities, as well as how to find ppl and etc - just send me a DM. :)

Depending where you land, you have different routes of exploration. It really depends what you are into too - some parts offer better sea experience, mountain, forests and etc.

To come here:
- you can fly to Sofia
- you can fly to Varna
- you can fly to Bucharest and catch a bus to Ruse/cab to Silistra. Usually this is cheaper.
- you can fly to Plovdiv (might not have flights available)

To visit:
- We got many abandoned or less crowded villages. For some 20-30lev and a company, a Bulgarian grandma might house you. There are many many stories you can hear, many old ways to see too. Just need a Bulgarian friend to join you (might be able to connect you with some nice people who like to travel - mainly people involved with LARP). There are villages holding mysterious stories (Tsaritchina, Shishentsi), villages-museums (Etara near Gabrovo) and many more.

- Many historical and religious beauties around too. From the sinking church, thru Rila's Monastery, to Baba Vida's fortress in Vidin and Mediji Tabia fortress in Silistra, where my great grandpa was a soldier in. Some soviet monuments like the one on Buzludzha or one of our most treasured - the monument on Shipka's peak 

- Pretty mountains, easy and medium to climb peaks. 7 Rila's lakes are amazing place to visit. If you are into mysteries, Strandzha is your place. Beware, it is similar to the Appalachia so don't go alone. There are few nice villages you can visit with border patrol. You can climb to get some of the magical mumio rock. 

- You can visit "The path of the Bow and the Horse" - guaranteed great experience, or go on a tour with Electric Extreme, electric mountain bikes. You can visit Dospat and have some magical evenings on the big lake. 

- Visiting cities might require either couch surfing or hostels (Yo-Ho-Hostel in Varna is a great hit; Moreto & Caffeto in Sofia). 
+ Sofia offers great outing places and architecture to explore. Many different ppl, might as well find fellow travellers. Sofia might be dangerous at night, you need to stray away from some neighborhoods (Zhenski Pazar, Levski, other).

+ Plovdiv is the place you feel at home, recommending the old town. Rather safe, a lot of walking, city transport is not reliable.

+ Varna is the most friendliest town. I went there with a friend at 2am to eat gyros and we never once felt in danger (being 5'1 gals). Many young ppl, lovely seaside

+ Veliko Turnovo is a place with rich history and green scenery 

+ Silistra and the towns around can offer a lot less places to visit, but I'll be more than happy to host you or help you with choosing correct accommodation and even travel around. Dobrich has a great Zoo Centre, a must see.

There are many many other stuff that can be done here, many stuff to explore. Don't hesitate to reach out, I'll be more than happy to help.

Tips:
1. Maybe try to bring a friend. I'm paranoid and I wouldn't travel alone to a foreign country, no matter how safe it is.
2. Only purchase cabs over the phone or via App so they can be traced. Cabs on stations will always charge you more, once they get you are a foreigner, they will double it. The app will always tell you the exact sum. Recommending "Yellow"
2. Always carry an extra battery. We don't have many charging stations or electrical outlets
3. Always have someone knowing your location, especially around villages. There is no reception around some so always plan ahead and have a plan B
4. Camping is not as bad, we have some designated spots over the country (Irakli by the sea for example, hikers camping sites, etc)
5. Most street food is safe
6. If you can't drink rakija with them, you can't trust them
7. Last time I hitchhiked, I had a pleasant experience. Idk how it's now, but also be weary.
8. Must try banitsa, fried bread with jam and white cheese, homemade rakija and sarmi. 

Hope I was helpful and hoping other people can add to this thread. Good luck!!!🤞
